structured_output.hypothesis: In a global fossil occurrence database, the taxonomic similarity (shared genera) between faunas of consecutive geological stages is much higher than between stages widely separated in time, and a stage's fauna is on average more similar to its neighbours than to the stages on either side of them.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using marine animal genera from PBDB occurrences binned by international stage (Cambrian to Neogene, bins with at least 50 genera), compute pairwise Jaccard similarity of genus sets. Pass if (a) mean Jaccard at lag 1 (consecutive stages) is at least 2.0 times mean Jaccard at lag 10 or more stages, AND (b) the Spearman correlation between lag (1 to 20 stages) and Jaccard is -0.5 or lower with p < 0.01, AND (c) for at least 80% of stage triplets (A,B,C) in succession, J(A,B) and J(B,C) both exceed J(A,C) (the intermediate-fauna test).
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fail if the lag-1 to lag-10+ mean Jaccard ratio is below 1.5, OR the Spearman correlation between lag and Jaccard is above -0.3, OR fewer than 60% of triplets satisfy J(A,B) > J(A,C) and J(B,C) > J(A,C). Results between these bounds count as inconclusive and are not support.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'formations' are mapped to the international chronostratigraphic stages recorded in PBDB (early_interval and late_interval). 'Fossils' are mapped to genus-level taxa. 'Closely related' is measured as the Jaccard overlap of genus sets, with sampling standardisation (subsampling to equal occurrence counts per stage) as a robustness check. Darwin meant taxonomic affinity (shared or closely allied species and genera), so genus overlap is a modern proxy. 'Far more' is operationalised as at least a 2x ratio. Known confounds: turnover rates and sampling vary through time, and mass extinctions will lower lag-1 similarity at some boundaries. The claim is tested as a general pattern, so a few exceptional boundaries are allowed by the 80% triplet threshold.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB holds global fossil collection and occurrence records with taxonomic identification and stratigraphic age assignment. Its public data service API (paleobiodb.org/data1.2/occs/list.csv) allows bulk download. Fields that would be used: accepted_name or genus, early_interval, late_interval, max_ma, min_ma, and phylum, class and environment for filtering to marine animals. These allow per-stage genus sets and pairwise similarity by stage separation to be computed.
